summary: Source cleanup under the rule that encyclopedias, newsletters, advocacy trackers, association and trade-group summaries, and a litigant's own advocacy page are leads, never sources. A scan of every record found such sources in 25 records. Where nothing relied on them they were removed (7 records). Where they backed events or text, research subagents opened replacements (court orders on court sites and storage.courtlistener.com, agency releases, White House staff reports and signing notices, CRS reports, and wire-service and trade-press reports), and three independent reviewers re-opened them and rewrote 18 records. Scanned copies of official documents that associations or trackers host were kept as identified third-party copies. Facts that no opened source supported were moved to uncertainties as unverified, and events that rested only on newsletters, an analyst's dashboard, an encyclopedia date or an association summary were removed (c01-04, c02-04, c05-10, c05-11, c11-20). Corrections found on the way: the Defense Department indirect-cost cap was held unlawful on summary judgment on 2025-10-10 and the no-petition date is 2026-04-09 (c11-12); the 2025 Congressional Review Act signing covered four BLM plans or amendments and one leasing record of decision (c02-07); the Energy Secretary described planned tests as system tests, not nuclear explosions (c04-06, AP, 2025-11-02); the D.C. Circuit's USIP stay order of 2025-06-27 now backs that record's court status (c03-09). No stage changed. Confidence moved on two records: c03-09 up (70 to 72), c05-27 down (80 to 79, its deciding memorandum is a third-party copy). Counts unchanged: 115 in effect of 627 counted.
title: Source cleanup over 25 records
